Which era in the Geological Time Scale covers the greatest duration of time?
Cenozoic
Mesozoic
Neoproterozoic
Palaeozoic

Which of the following is correctly ordered from oldest to youngest?
Silurian, Paleogene, Cambrian, Jurassic
Ordovician, Devonian, Triassic, Cretaceous
Archaean, Hadean, Proterozoic, Phanerozoic
Cenozoic, Mesozoic, Palaeozoic, Neoproterozoic

Significant increases in oxygen in the atmosphere occurred during the Precambrian. Which sphere was largely responsible for this increase in the production of oxygen?
Atmosphere
Biosphere
Geosphere
Hydrosphere

Which of the following is made from a renewable resource?
Cardboard
Glass
Petrol
Steel – 3 –

The principle of uniformitarianism states that geological processes acted
in an unexplained manner in the past.
randomly in the past as they do in the present.
in the same manner and with the same intensity in the past as they do at present.
in a different manner and with a different intensity in the past as they do at present.

Which of the following is most likely to account for the origin of life on Earth?
Panspermia
Superposition
Continental drift
Anthropogenesis

At which of the following tectonic boundaries do most earthquakes of high magnitude occur?
Oceanic–oceanic divergent
Continental–oceanic convergent
Continental–continental divergent
Continental–continental convergent

Which of the following is the best technique that could be used to project how Earth’s climate will change in the future?
Analysing ice cores
Forecasting daily weather
Extrapolating past climate data
Using computers to model climate processes

Which of the following identifies the potential immediate hazards caused by explosive volcanic eruptions such as those associated with Mount Pinatubo?
Pyroclastic flows, lahars, acid rain, typhoons
Earthquakes, typhoons, lava bombs, ash emissions
Lahars, poisonous gas emissions, lava bombs, ash emissions
Poisonous gas emissions, global warming, lava bombs, ash emissions – 4 –

Australia may be susceptible to a tsunami because it
is on a convergent plate boundary.
is near active plate boundaries in New Zealand.
has a divergent boundary to the south of Tasmania.
has large tidal movements around the north of the continent.

Which human activity has the most immediate and direct effect on natural habitats?
Over-harvesting fish for human consumption
Combustion of fossil fuels producing carbon dioxide
Urban expansion requiring infrastructure development
Coal fired power stations producing thermal pollution in artificial lakes

Which of the following contributes most to the enhanced greenhouse effect?
Carbon
Methane
Nitrogen
Oxygen – 5 – Refer to the following graph to answer Questions 13 and 14. The projections are derived from different greenhouse gas emission scenarios. Earth’s average global temperature between 1900 and 2008 was approximately 15°C. If the world follows a lower emissions scenario (X), what would the average global temperature in 2100 be closest to?
2°C
4°C
16°C
17°C

Which aspect of the graph shows the scientific uncertainty associated with each projection?
The shading around each line
The time scale shown in 25 year intervals
Showing both observations and a trend line
Many data points shown on the same graph – 6 –
